clue.text: English lines set to piano by church composer

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
URC stands for the United Reformed Church, a British Protestant denomination
L is short for line, so LL means lines

explanation.surface: A church composer sets some English verse to piano accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church composer' looks like the definition, but 'church' gives URC (the United Reformed Church, a British denomination); the English and lines go after the piano and church.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Purcell was a celebrated English Baroque composer, so the name is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Good example of pressure on old kingdom

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the pressure letter on top of the kingdom

parts.note: P is the scientific abbreviation for pressure
Aragon was a medieval kingdom in Spain

explanation.surface: A model case of pressure applied to an ancient realm.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, a perfect example.

clue.text: Procedure for dealing with letters arranged by nicer editor

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Mail-handling methods are organised by a pleasanter editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges NICER EDITOR; 'by' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Redirection is the forwarding of mail to a new address, a postal procedure.

clue.text: Custodian of French art and gold kept by court

parts.note: es is French for 'art' in the old sense of 'thou art', you are

indicators.note: kept by means the gold goes inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A guardian of French artworks keeps gold in a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is not painting: it is the archaic verb, as in 'thou art', which is 'tu es' in French.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a guard or protector who accompanies someone, a kind of custodian.

clue.text: Wrap, one with diamonds and stars —- gems cut by them?

parts.note: to lap is to wrap or fold around
I is the Roman numeral for one
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: A gift is wrapped with diamonds and stars, prompting a thought about the gem cutters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads back through the clue: those who cut gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapidaries are craftsmen who cut and polish precious stones.

clue.text: Beast-in short man about to create trouble

indicators.note: about says the whole combination of beast and man is turned round
in short says the word for beast loses its final letter

parts.note: a brute is a beast
Sid is a man's name

explanation.surface: A brute of a little man is about to stir up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' cuts BRUTE to BRUT; add SID and 'about' turns BRUTSID backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb is to unsettle or upset things, so it is to create trouble.

clue.text: One like Mary with no time to be a Martha?

indicators.note: with no time means the abbreviation for time is taken out

parts.note: in the Gospel, Mary sat adoringly at Jesus's feet, so she is a doter

explanation.surface: Someone like Mary has no time to be a busy Martha.
explanation.walkthrough: In Luke's Gospel Martha bustles about serving while her sister Mary sits listening to Jesus; DOTER loses T.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha is the biblical type of the busy, practical person, someone who gets things done.

clue.text: Drink made stronger and drawn off by tube

parts.note: to sip is to drink
honed means sharpened or strengthened

explanation.surface: A drink made more potent is sucked out through a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To siphon liquid is to draw it off through a tube.

clue.text: A single Spanish lady

definitions.meaning: ... is the Spanish feminine word for a or one

explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish the feminine form for one is una, and Una is also a female first name.

clue.text: Insect is big brute a husband avoided

indicators.note: avoided means the husband letter is left out

parts.note: a behemoth is a huge beast

explanation.surface: An insect is a huge monster that a husband steers clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: A bee moth is a moth whose larvae live in beehives, an insect.

clue.text: Little boy is a Pole

definitions.meaning: The familiar short form of the boy's name Rodney

explanation.definitionFit: Rod is a shortened boy's name, and a rod is a long thin pole.

clue.text: Officer by river to give a hand

parts.note: a copper is slang for a police officer
the Plate is the River Plate in South America

explanation.surface: A police officer by a river offers someone a helping hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' here means handwriting, not helping, and 'to give' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Copperplate is an elegant style of joined-up writing, and a hand is a style of handwriting.

clue.text: Queen to become disrespectful about King

indicators.note: about means the phrase for growing disrespectful goes round the letter for king

parts.note: to get rude is to become disrespectful
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A queen grows impertinent towards the king.
explanation.walkthrough: GET RUDE goes round R. Gertrude is the queen in Shakespeare's Hamlet, which suits a royal surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude is the Queen of Denmark, Hamlet's mother, in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Surrender in respect of self esteem

parts.note: for can mean in respect of, as in 'for my part'
ego is a person's sense of self-worth

explanation.surface: Someone gives up their pride for the sake of a principle.
explanation.definitionFit: To forego, a variant spelling of forgo, is to give up or relinquish something, so to surrender it.

clue.text: Listen to bore with a beard, a very keen type

indicators.note: Listen to says the boring tool is heard rather than seen

parts.note: an auger is a tool for boring holes
beaver is old slang for a beard

explanation.surface: Hear out a tedious, bearded person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull person but is the drilling tool, AUGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An eager beaver is an idiom for an enthusiastic, hard-working person.

clue.text: Fantastic sand — please go to seaside resorts for such

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly altered, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Wonderful sand, so please visit the coast for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' rearranges SAND and PLEASE; 'go to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Esplanades are seafront promenades, features that seaside resorts are visited for.

clue.text: Site of shrine said to be something groovy

indicators.note: said tells us the place name is heard, not seen, giving a different spelling

parts.note: Knock in County Mayo, Ireland, is the site of a famous Marian shrine

explanation.surface: A holy place is supposedly rather fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groovy' looks like slang for trendy, but it literally means having a groove.
explanation.definitionFit: A nock is the notch at the end of an arrow or bow, literally a grooved feature.

clue.text: Held in reserve at this yard? Not quite

definitions.text: Held in reserve at this yard? Not quite

parts.words: Held in reserve at this yard? Not quite
parts.note: the idiom for keeping someone at a distance describes a span from shoulder to fingertip, roughly but not quite a yard

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means held at a distance or in reserve; a person's reach is a bit under a yard (about 91 cm).
explanation.definitionFit: To keep someone at arm's length is to keep them at a cool, reserved distance.

clue.text: Tissue and fabric found around pool maybe

indicators.note: found around means the fabric surrounds the game

parts.note: lint is a soft fabric for dressing wounds
pool is an example of a game

explanation.surface: Tissue and fabric are discovered near a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' is not water but the cue game.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is a band of fibrous tissue linking bones.

clue.text: As vivacious types, pity idlers in need of reform

indicators.note: in need of reform says these letters must be reorganised

explanation.surface: Lively people find lazy loafers pitiful and in need of correction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of reform' rearranges the ten letters of PITY IDLERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting spiritedly means behaving with liveliness, as vivacious people do.

clue.text: Mum's in hut completely sozzled

indicators.note: in means mum's goes inside the hut

parts.note: a shed is a hut
ma is mum, so Mum's gives the letters for ma's

explanation.surface: Mother is in the shed, totally drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashed is slang for very drunk, as is sozzled.

clue.text: Items in womenswear making endless money

indicators.note: endless says the slang word for cash loses its last letter

parts.note: brass is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Women's clothing items bring in unending cash.
explanation.walkthrough: BRASS, British slang for money, loses its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Bras are undergarments, items found among women's clothing.

clue.text: Ruin brought by drink restricting working team

indicators.note: restricting means the drink contains the team

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a crew is a team of workers

explanation.surface: Disaster follows when drink hampers a work crew.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw up is a colloquial way to spoil or ruin something.

clue.text: Greek character with no head and hardly any length

indicators.note: with no head means the first letter goes

parts.note: omicron is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A headless Greek figure of almost no stature.
explanation.definitionFit: A micron is a millionth of a metre, a tiny length.

clue.text: See girl confronting gangster get tough

indicators.note: confronting means standing in front of, so the girl comes before the gangster

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Watch a girl stand up to a gangster and turn hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is just an opening link.
explanation.definitionFit: To anneal metal or glass is to heat and cool it so that it becomes tougher and less brittle.

clue.text: Plot always found at the back of English home

indicators.note: at the back of puts the word for always after the other pieces

parts.note: in means at home
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A conspiracy is forever discovered behind an English house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer something is to contrive or scheme it, so to plot it.

clue.text: Good valuable stuff from part of Kensington

parts.note: ore is mineral rock worth mining

explanation.surface: Good valuable goods come from a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Kensington Gore is a street in Kensington, London, by the Royal Albert Hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Kensington Gore is a road in west London, so Gore names a part of Kensington.

clue.text: Thou seemest to be such a resident

definitions.text: Thou seemest to be such a resident

parts.words: Thou seemest to be such a resident
parts.note: the words Thou seemest physically hold, inside them, the letters of a word for a dwelling, so they act as its container; read as a phrase, a resident is someone who occupies a home

explanation.walkthrough: Look across the join of 'Thou seemest' to find a word for a dwelling sitting inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A householder is a person who occupies or owns a dwelling, a resident of it.

clue.text: Stream lacking breadth needed for vessel

indicators.note: lacking means the breadth letter is taken out

parts.note: a burn is a Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: A narrow stream is needed to fill a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase or container, a vessel.

clue.text: Promise in certain letters only half fulfilled

indicators.note: only half fulfilled means we keep just the first half of the word for those letters

parts.note: vowels are certain letters of the alphabet: a, e, i, o, u

explanation.surface: A pledge in some correspondence was kept only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: VOWELS keeps only its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A vow is a solemn promise.

clue.text: Small room with lots of noise character dropping hands at sides

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

indicators.note: dropping hands at sides means removing the two letters for left and right hands from each end

parts.note: a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: A small, noisy room has someone with arms hanging down.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R stand for left and right hands, removed from the ends of LETTER to leave ETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinette is a small dining room or eating area.

clue.text: Region with students returning where it's pleasantly warm

indicators.note: returning says the region and students are read backwards together

parts.note: a part is a region or area
NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain

explanation.surface: Students come back to an area that enjoys pleasant warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses PARTNUS. NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK students' organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A suntrap is a sheltered sunny spot, a place where it is pleasantly warm.
